prerequisites: Knowledge of High School Maths concepts.
Ability to correctly use such concepts in calculus.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of basic notions and laws of Mechanics and Thermodynamics, as indicated in the course program.
Ability to schematize physical systems and phenomena.
Ability to apply the basic laws of Mechanics and Thermodynamics to physical situations and to perform the related operations and calculations.
Ability to critically evaluate the outcome of problems.
Ability to logically present demonstrations of Mechanics and Thermodynamics.

syllabus_topics: Operations with vectors: Sum, Difference, Scalar Product, Vector Product
Cartesian reference frames and orthogonal axes
From acceleration to the equation of motion: the integration process
Tangential and centripetal acceleration in curvilinear motion
The fundamental problem of dynamics: from forces to motion
Relative motion reference systems: relationship between speed and acceleration measured in two reference systems
Work of a force: definition and unit of measure
The first cardinal equation of dynamic systems
Second cardinal equation of dynamic systems
Kinetic energy theorem for a system of material points
Energy Conservation for Material Point Systems
Kinetic energy of a rigid body rotating around a fixed axis
Pressure: definition and unit of measurement
Joule's experiences: work, heat, internal energy: first principle of thermodynamics
Equation of state of ideal gases
Internal energy of a perfect gas
Mayer's relationship between specific heat at constant volume and pressure of a perfect gas
Isobaric, isochoric, isothermal, adiabatic transformations of the ideal gas
Second law of thermodynamics: Clausius and Kelvin-Planck statements and their equivalence
assessment_rules: The exam consists of written and oral components. The oral exam is mandatory and requires a score of eighteen or higher on the written exam to be eligible. The final mark is given by the synthesis of the two marks obtained in these partial tests. Honors (Laude) is awarded for work or performance distinguished by brilliance and originality, exceeding standard curricular expectations.
